correctness.rationale: The frozen proof counts distinct classes, including zero once. An odd-prime square has even valuation and square leading unit, and these conditions suffice by lifting. For nonzero shift of valuation t, classes below t keep their leading unit, classes above t obtain the shift's leading unit, and at t the only cancellation is at the unique leading residue −u. Away from 0 and −u the two nonzero unit tests reduce exactly to the finite-field character count; the quadratic character sum is −1 by counting factorizations of u². When t is even the two tail counts coincide by scaling by p^t. Odd t leaves only the lower layers; h=0 returns the cardinality. CRT acts on both membership tests. For p≡1 mod 4 the difference is 2S_{p,m}(1)−p^{m−1}, equal to 1 at m=1 and strictly negative by the geometric bound for p≥5, m≥2. Independent direct sets checked 1,555 prime-power shifts and all 780 shifts over six stated composites, and recovered the prime-five pairs (2,1),(2,5),(6,25),(22,125). evidence: Put r=m−v for the frequency's conductor exponent. On units modulo p^r, both the constant and Legendre-character exponential sums vanish for r>t+1. At r=t+1 they equal −p^t and p^t T_p χ(u). Thus only the last surviving conductor can depend on the character of u.

For r≤t, including frequency zero, Parseval on the reduction modulo p^t gives the partial inverse sum U_{p,m}(t)+p^{t−m}S_{p,m}(t)^2: the nonzero fibers below t have size p^{m−t} and the zero fiber has size S_{p,m}(t). This includes the trivial reduction at t=0.

Write B=S_{p,m}(t+1), P=p^{m−t−1}. If t is odd, the prior J at r=t+1 is B and cancels the squared zero-fiber term. If t is even, the prior J=B−P/2 ± PT_p/2; substituting and using S_{p,m}(t)=B+(p−1)P/2 gives U+B+(p−3)P/4 plus χ(u)(B−P/2) for p≡1 mod 4, and no character term for p≡3 mod 4. This is exactly the frozen formula since both scaled tails are B.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: At t=0 the difference is directly 2B−P. The known one-point tail gives +1 at depth one and a strict negative difference thereafter.
